classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate a height formula, then use the maximum launch velocity and the return-to-sea-level condition to solve a quadratic and interpret its positive root.

content.prompt: The height, $h$ metres above sea level, to which a rocket has risen $t$ seconds after launching from sea level is given by $h=ut-4.9t^2$, where $u$ metres per second is the launch velocity.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the height above sea level 4 seconds after the launch of a rocket with a launch velocity of 115 m/s.

answer.worked:
Substitute $u=115$ and $t=4$:
$$\begin{align*}h&=115(4)-4.9(4)^2\\h&=460-78.4\\h&=381.6\end{align*}$$
The height above sea level is $381.6\text{ m}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
If the launch velocity can be a maximum of 500 m/s, calculate the longest possible time of flight, to the nearest second.

(Hint: At the end of a flight, the height above sea level is 0 m.)

answer.worked:
Use the maximum launch velocity, $u=500$, and set $h=0$:
$$\begin{align*}500t-4.9t^2&=0\\t(500-4.9t)&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus $t=0$ or
$$\begin{align*}500-4.9t&=0\\4.9t&=500\\t&=\frac{5000}{49}\\t&\approx102.0408\end{align*}$$
The root $t=0$ is the launch time. The longest possible time of flight is $102\text{ seconds}$, to the nearest second.
